Theme

Household, washing & chores

servant noun

also servants, maid, maidservant, manservant, domestic servant, attendant, the servants

classical

Cic. Off. 2.24: ut herīs in famulōs (Lewis & Short)
Verg. A. 1.701

famulus, famulī m.; famula, famulae f.

servant, attendant; maid (famula)

The member of a household who serves (the word that gave familia). In Rome a house servant was normally a slave, so the classical words cover that too; for a slave as such, servus; for someone paid, see employee.

Other words

  • minister, ministrī m. — attendant, servant who waits on someone

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Verg. A. 1.705 (Lewis & Short); Catull. 27.1 (Lewis & Short)

    One who serves at hand: at table, at a sacrifice, in an office; then any helper or agent. Not a government minister classically (see minister).

  • ancilla, ancillae f. — maid, maidservant

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Plaut. Mil. 3.1.199: ecqua ancilla est illī? (Lewis & Short); Cic. Off. 1.113 (Lewis & Short)

    The usual classical word for a woman servant, as the feminine of servus.

Examples

  • dant famulī manibus lymphās Cereremque canistrīs expediunt

    the servants pour water on their hands and serve bread from the basketsVerg. A. 1.701–702

  • et clārā famulam poscit mortāria vōce

    and he calls loudly to the maid for the mortarMor. 93

See also employee, civil servant, serve, waiter, minister.
